text:
bryan: kicking off a short sync on the telemetry/console PRD — specifically retention UX + trace sampling + acceptance criteria. link to draft: https://redwood.internal/docs/telemetry-console-prd (WIP)

julie: skimmed — big +1 on carving out clear rollout gates. do we have perf targets yet?

bryan: not finalized. proposal in doc: SLOs + rollout checks. rough targets: dashboard queries p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for typical queries. need to validate with eng infra.

omar: from design: we should avoid a deep settings page. propose a compact retention control with presets (30/90/365) + a custom field. warn when >365. add inline cost estimate. mock attached in doc.

dmitri: perf targets look reasonable but depends on retention tier. long retention means more index scanning for range queries. can we limit query date window by default to 30d in UI to keep p95 low?

rachael: also want acceptance criteria for trace sampling semantics. customers asked for deterministic sampling by service + rate. need FR: ability to set sampling per-tenant, per-service, and a global default.

julie: re: sampling — runtime will support probabilistic and deterministic. need API + UI to set `sampling.policy = {type: 'prob', rate: 0.05}` or `{type: 'det', key: 'request_id', rate: 0.01}`. add to PRD.

bryan: adding to doc: "Acceptance checklist" draft. please sanity-check and add items.

omar: UI acceptance items from design: 1) retention picker shows cost delta, 2) preview of data retained, 3) warning modal for >180d, 4) trace detail page shows sampling rate and reason.

julie: engineering acceptance: 1) end-to-end tests covering retention change backfill job, 2) canary on internal beta with 5% tenants, 3) dashboard query latency within SLOs for 95% of queries during canary, 4) no data loss on rollback.

dmitri: add infra ops: migration job must be idempotent and rate-limited. backfill plan: background worker that processes tenant-by-tenant with checkpointing. CLI snippet for running backfill:```/bin/rw-backfill --tenant $TENANT --from 0 --to NOW --batch 10k```

rachael: edge cases to call out in PRD: exported archives (if customer exports old traces, retention policy should not delete exported copies), cross-region traces (follow data residency), and archived models referencing traces.

bryan: good list. also need launch metrics: retention tier adoption %, rollback rate, mean query latency, cost delta per 100k queries. add as M0 metrics.

omar: UX flow question: when a tenant increases retention, do we trigger an explicit backfill job or run a lazy backfill on first query? pros/cons?

julie: lazy backfill avoids heavy immediate load but gives inconsistent results. explicit backfill gives deterministic behavior but spikes cost. propose hybrid: schedule background backfill at low priority, and lazy on-demand for queries older than backfill checkpoint but show partial results message in UI. add to doc.

dmitri: hybrid seems safest. add circuit-breaker: if backfill exceeds X tokens or time, pause and alert on-call.

deploy-bot: doc updated: telemetry-console-prd-draft.md uploaded by bryan at 2026-05-12T14:11:29Z

bryan: request for PM review: tagging @julie @omar @dmitri — please add specific acceptance test steps (not just high level). e.g., exact queries to run, sample tenant ids, scripts.

omar: will put UX test steps: run through retention change, confirm warning modal, check cost estimate, inspect trace detail sampling display.

julie: I'll add automation test plan and a block of curl commands for API test harness. example:```curl -X POST /api/v1/tenants/123/settings -d '{"retention_days":90}'``` then run `make integration-test` to validate backfill job behavior.

rachael: I'll draft evaluation scenarios for sampling regressions — ensure fidelity of sampled traces against full set via offline eval. include sample dataset and thresholds.

bryan: decision needed on scope: do we ship both per-service sampling controls and per-tenant retention at GA? engineering capacity might push per-service sampling to next milestone. thoughts?

julie: prefer to ship per-tenant sampling + global defaults for GA. per-service adds complexity to runtime routing and UI. can be v1.1.

omar: agree. keep UI simple for GA. we can expose per-service via API for advanced users but hide in UI until v1.1.

dmitri: ok from infra POV. will need a follow-up RFC for per-service policy and how to route at inference time.

bryan: consensus: GA = retention tiers + per-tenant sampling + hybrid backfill + rollout gates. per-service sampling moved to follow-up. I'll update PRD and mark requirements and acceptance criteria accordingly.

julie: sgtm. timeline note: aiming for feature freeze in 4 weeks, canary in 6 weeks.

rachael: flagged risk: observability costs could increase ~30% for 365d tier in our estimates. add cost mitigation ideas: aggregation, downsampling, sampling higher for archive tiers.

bryan: thanks — please append mitigation proposals to doc. I'll call a 20-min sync tomorrow to finalize acceptance list.

omar: +1. I'll bring mocks.

julie: tagging follow-ups in the doc under /acceptance-tests. everyone please add specific steps by EOD.
